evidence.exact_quote:
1. [GitButler timeline documentation](https://docs.gitbutler.com/features/timeline), S00004:30–39, promises undo of “nearly” any action, pre-major-action snapshots and occasional capture of recently changed uncommitted files. This does not establish continuous capture, every operation's recovery, or a complete repository backup.
2. [Oplog capture at `8861f862`](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/gitbutler-oplog/src/oplog.rs#L782-L962), S00021:782–962 / S00028, records index and optional index-conflict trees, target/conflict state, selected project metadata, branch order, virtual-branch state/commit bytes, worktree, optional additional ref and checkout identity, and the workspace commit independently of HEAD. `project_meta.toml` is selected target/ref/push-remote information (S00021:44–51), **not the full project database**. Lines 860–928 overlay graph-projected metadata through `set_workspace` and synchronize applied heads, so capture is not simply copying a stale TOML file. This also connects to the ownership lead below.
3. [Linked-worktree API](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/8861f862414df646220fc6f935b4ab404456d577/crates/but-api/src/worktrees.rs#L5-L10), S00022:5–10, expressly excludes its mutations from oplog: archive state is a project-database row and a removed checkout cannot be restored from a snapshot. Its feature gate is also explicit. This qualifies broad marketing wording; it does not prove that JJ shares these exact exclusions.

- **Native owner:** `Plans/Jujutsu_Integration.md:9–11,180–209` (JJI-005; S00003) explicitly separates `jj undo`/`jj op restore`, FileSafe decisions and receipts, and forbids recovery claims without post-restore snapshot/conflict proof. evidence.exact_quote:
No inspected passage proves a diagnostic/recovery implementation that remains usable when normal workspace projection fails. Conversely, nothing proves a JJ implementation has GitButler's bug: these are different native models, and the frozen Plans explicitly do not certify a running adapter. Therefore the aggregate remains **uncertain**, with its existing requirements preserved. No reported manual Git plumbing, `but teardown`, relaxed guard, automatic rewind or Git mutation fallback is recommended for JJ.

### Reviewable proposal: damaged-state diagnosis and fenced recovery

**Product proposal requiring approval; not an adopted policy.** Add an explicit degraded recovery path behind existing owner routes. When mutation or recovery cannot establish coherent state, retain the mutation fence and present a source-bound diagnostic receipt that distinguishes last verified state, observed per-domain progress and unknown domains. Read-only inspection should use native operation/store/workspace evidence independently of the normal healthy status projection where the certified adapter supports it. Failure to reconstruct current identity must return a typed unavailable diagnosis; it must not invent an expected revision, bypass the writer fence, or mutate to make diagnosis succeed. Any later recovery still needs an exact observed-state precondition, owner confirmation, preserved dirty state and independent postcondition checks.

Benefit: an operation error need not strand the user behind the same status/capture precondition that failed. Dependencies: JJI-002/005, neutral writer-lease recovery, certified native read modes, source-bound diagnostic retention, FileSafe for external file effects, and existing UI/ObservableWork/Backup owner routes. Tradeoffs: extra diagnosis/storage cost and potentially prolonged quarantine; some corrupt states cannot be repaired automatically. **Material choice to review:** retain quarantine plus explicit recovery as the first policy, or add eagerly published pre-mutation checkpoints and automatic rollback for narrowly certified operation classes. Automatic rollback needs additional capture/publication guarantees, external-writer handling and performance/retention decisions; this evidence does not authorize it. A full raw-storage recovery-copy feature would additionally need Backup ownership and scope approval, not a new JJ-private backup facility.

**Partial integration and recovery preconditions.** Uncertain upstream aggregate; covered no-blind-retry/fenced-recovery principles plus an unapproved damaged-state diagnosis proposal. Fault injection must include failure obtaining normal workspace projection or before-state capture. Preserve observed partial effects and unknown domains; no invented coherent after revision, relaxed guard or fallback Git mutation. Primary sources: S00009/S00010, S00031, S00035, S00033, S00054/S00056/S00058.

evidence.exact_quote:
[Issue #15573](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/issues/15573), S00011:145–175, reports 0.22.1/Linux and an eight-segment restore that rewound only the tip while seven lower refs remained on the abandoned chain. At lines 198–216 the author explicitly marks the SQLite-versus-TOML explanation as a guess. Do not retain that guess as the root cause.

[Merged PR #15584](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/pull/15584), S00030 (`merged=true`, merge `a8cca1862e8cd67b1d91d0c1361d32adca401961`, 2026-08-27 08:08:16 UTC), explicitly fixes #15573. Its primary explanation (S00008:147–158) identifies global lowest-order name matching that moved owned heads into a stale stack during `set_workspace`. UI remained correct because it used the ref graph; capture used degraded metadata; restore followed applied ownership. Duplicates are ownership entries across stacks, not multiple same-full-name Git refs.

[Code at the merge](https://github.com/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/blob/a8cca1862e8cd67b1d91d0c1361d32adca401961/crates/but-meta/src/legacy/mod.rs#L483-L558), S00024:483–558, preserves incoming existing stack identity and calls `stack_has_head` before global fallback. [Patch tests](https://api.github.com/repos/gitbutlerapp/gitbutler/pulls/15584/files), S00020, roundtrip synthetic metadata in `duplicate_names_in_unapplied_stacks_do_not_steal_applied_branches` and `shared_segment_names_stay_in_their_own_applied_stacks`. Applied and stale owners retain their own entries/OIDs; legitimate cross-stack movement can still use fallback. These tests were inspected, not run, and are not an eight-segment live restore demonstration. Blanket duplicate-name rejection would reject supported states.
